Alex.confusing: The dawn egg rules were hard to track: the Turkey gains an egg only from visitors, and Casey's Owl read on Ellis showed how easily a flat nest gets misread at the table.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when the table converged on Blair and Blair's shifting visit story unravelled in front of everyone. Watching the claims contradict each other was the most engaging part of the game.
Alex.change: I'd spell out the visitor-versus-host egg direction for every animal in the rules, since several players, including me, got it backwards mid-day.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw my whole nest of 10 cards at Blair on the table's consensus without verifying who visited Ellis. Knowing Ellis was the Floofer, I'd have tested Ellis directly and thrown fewer cards.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were easy to misread: the table argued for a round over whether the Turkey or the visitor gains the egg, and I couldn't tell until someone corrected it.
Blair.fun: Round 1 as the Sphinx was great: Drew and Ellis both publicly endorsed my cover story, and then my 5-card throw at Alex flipped the vote to Meowfia.
Blair.change: Spell out the egg mechanics for Turkey, Owl and Falcon in the dawn report, so players don't argue over the rules instead of the roles.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I threw my last two cards at Casey, a Farm player, and that only added a couple of votes to a loss. I should have kept my 10 and waited for a better throw.

Casey.confusing: The Owl's dawn report never said which animals visited my target, so my "someone else visited" read couldn't name anyone. I also didn't know a Floofer could hug visitors and leave the nest flat.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when Blair's shifting story pulled the table together and Blair was eggsecuted as Meowfia. My Owl read helped build that case.
Casey.change: Have the Owl's dawn report name the animals that visited the target, as the role text says, so Owl reads are checkable.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I threw at Blair (Farm, the Hawk) on the strength of a visitor I couldn't name, when Ellis, the Floofer, was the hidden Meowfia I should have pressed. I would throw at Ellis instead and ask Ellis directly about the unexplained visit.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey rule was easy to misread: I first thought the Turkey gained the egg, but the visitor gains it, which I got backwards on the table.
Drew.fun: Round 2 went well: Blair was the Meowfia and I helped vote them out at 8 votes to 2 after the table pressed on their shifting visit story.
Drew.change: I'd make the Turkey and Owl egg rules spelled out in the dawn report, since they're easy to misread and it's hard to check claims against them.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I threw at Blair, who was Farm, instead of Ellis, the Floofer Meowfia whose unexplained visit I should have pressed harder. I'd have pushed to vote Ellis.

Ellis.confusing: The Storyteller's dawn reports and the role-changing rules were the hardest part, since Turkey and Hawk payouts depend on who visited whom and the reports didn't always say. Several players, including me, got the Turkey and Falcon egg rules wrong at first.
Ellis.fun: Round 2's vote, where the table split on Blair and I threw alongside Drew, Finley and Casey to get the Meowfia out. Nobody could verify the claims, so the day turned on who sounded consistent.
Ellis.change: Publish a clear visit log to every player at dawn, so claims like Owl and Falcon can be checked instead of argued.
Ellis.regret: In round 3, as Floofer, I invented a Pigeon visit on Finley to cover my hug, which only muddied the day. I would have stayed quiet or stuck to the true hug, since a false visit claim gave Casey's accusation room to stand.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey and Falcon egg rules caused real confusion on the table, since several players first said the Turkey gets the egg when the visitor does. Nothing in the dawn reports explained who visited whom, so the table kept guessing about the Ellis visit.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was fun: Blair's shifting visit stories drew three throws in one beat, and the table converged fast on the Meowfia.
Finley.change: Have dawn reports name the visitors (or at least how many) to the target, so the table can check claims against the egg counts instead of arguing over them.
Finley.regret: In Round 1 I falsely claimed to be the Hawk and pushed suspicion onto Alex, a Farm player. In Round 3 I threw my cards at Blair, who was Farm, when I should have looked harder at Ellis, the Floofer who was actually Meowfia.
